AXP.rationale: American Express shows solid fundamental health with consistent revenue and EPS growth (Q1 2026 revenue $10.52B, EPS $4.28, YoY revenue +9.3%, EPS +17.6%), strong ROE of 33%, and a net margin of 26.6%. The closed-loop business model provides competitive advantages with premium customer base and high spending per cardmember. However, operating cash flow declined 20.2% YoY in Q1 2026, and the balance sheet shows elevated debt-to-equity of 1.73. Valuation is moderate with P/E of 21.5x, which is near the middle of its 1-year range (18.4-25.3x) and not particularly cheap versus history. The upcoming Q2 2026 earnings on July 24 provides a near-term catalyst with consensus EPS of $4.39 (+7.6% YoY), and the company has beaten estimates in 3 of 4 recent quarters. The 16% dividend increase and strong stress test results (2.5% SCB maintained) support capital return confidence. However, the stock has already rallied 16.8% in the past quarter, partially reflecting positive expectations. The score reflects a fundamentally sound franchise with decent but not exceptional valuation, modestly supported by the upcoming earnings event.
